sources.content:
# claude-toolkit

Personal Claude Code plugins, laid out as a private plugin marketplace. A proof of concept: it is compatible with the team-shared SDD skill but entirely separate from it, and never changes it. Every toolkit agent carries the `toolkit:` prefix.

## What it does

Two parts, installable separately. **[INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md) is the setup guide** (written so Claude Code can follow it for you).

1. **Claude sessions**: a "Claude sessions" view with the live, colour-coded status of every Claude session on the machine, a status-bar count, `Ctrl+Alt+N` to jump to waiting sessions, click-to-focus across VS Code windows, a `STATUS:` line at the end of every turn, and optionally a plain Claude tab that opens with a folder ("Toolkit: Open Claude here on startup"). Needs only the extension link and the status hooks.
2. **Coordinator**: open a project and a **coordinator** Claude session starts in an editor tab. It reports the SDD team recap, reads the project board and asks what is next. You tell it the goal; it creates the **worker** sessions the job needs, each in its own named tab with a written brief, and follows them through SendMessage. Workers that still have open work reopen with their conversation the next time you open the project. You can still type in any worker's tab.

| Part | Where |
|---|---|
| Status hooks (session events, `STATUS:` line instruction) and their installer | `status/` |
| `toolkit:coordinator` and `toolkit:worker` agents | `plugins/toolkit/agents/` |
| Start-up hook: runs SDD's team-mailbox pull for the coordinator only | `plugins/toolkit/hooks/` |
| VS Code extension: session view, plain Claude tab, coordinator and worker tabs | `vscode/` |

One project per coordinator; coordinating several projects is planned.

## Coordinator sessions

The extension starts every coordinator and worker session with `--plugin-dir <clone>/plugins/toolkit` and `--permission-mode auto` (sessions in the same mode exchange messages without approval prompts). `claude` must be on `PATH`, or set `claudeToolkit.claudePath`; `claudeToolkit.pluginDir` overrides the plugin folder. `claudeToolkit.workerLayout` chooses where worker tabs open: `beside` (default, the column next to the coordinator) or `tabs` (full-width tabs in the coordinator's column).

## Enable a project

Open the project folder and run "Toolkit: Enable coordinator in this folder". It records the folder as enabled on this machine (in the extension's own storage, never in the repository), creates `.coord/`, adds it to `.git/info/exclude` (never `.gitignore`), and opens the coordinator. From then on the coordinator opens whenever VS Code opens the folder; "Toolkit: Start coordinator" opens it again if you closed it. A repository that carries a `.coord/` folder starts nothing until you enable it yourself, and the extension's settings are machine-scoped, so a workspace cannot change which executable or plugin it runs.

### The board (`.coord/`)

| File | Written by | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| `team.json` | coordinator | `[{ "name", "role", "state": "active" \| "done" }]`; active workers reopen at start-up |
| `workers/<name>/brief.md` | coordinator | the worker's task |
| `workers/<name>/status.md` | worker | `State`, `Summary`, `Next` |
| `requests/<name>.json` | coordinator | `{ "name": "<name>" }`: asks the extension to open the worker; rejected requests leave `<name>.rejected.md` |
| `log.md` | coordinator | decisions, assignments and outcomes |
| `sessions/<session name>.id` | start-up hook | each worker's session ID, so its tab resumes exactly its own conversation, also when the coordinator requests a finished worker again |

Sessions are named `<project>-coordinator` and `<project>-<worker>` (the project folder name in lowercase, other characters as hyphens); tabs show the short name. Enabled projects need different folder names, or their sessions share names.

## Session status

The "Claude sessions" view (its own icon in the Activity Bar, the same in every window; drag it elsewhere once if you prefer) and the status-bar item show every interactive Claude Code session on this machine, toolkit or not. Clicking the status-bar item (`🔔 2 waiting`) shows the session waiting longest; `Ctrl+Alt+N` ("Toolkit: Next waiting session") cycles through the waiting sessions in urgency order; both reach tabs in other windows like a card click does.

| Colour | Status | Set by |
|---|---|---|
| red | waiting for permission / waiting for your answer | `PermissionRequest`; `AskUserQuestion`, or a turn ending with `STATUS: QUESTION` (coordinator and worker) or a final `?` |
| purple | possibly stuck | working with no event for `claudeToolkit.stuckMinutes` (default 10) |
| yellow | finished, needs review | any other end of turn |
| green | working | a prompt or a tool result |
| grey | idle | session started, no prompt yet |

Cards are grouped by project folder (each group shows how many of its sessions wait). Drag sessions within their project, and projects among projects, to arrange the view; your order is kept in every window and wins over urgency, while sessions and projects you never placed follow yours sorted by urgency (longest waiting first). "Move up" / "Move down" in a card's or project's context menu (also Shift+F10 from the keyboard) do the same without dragging. "Toolkit: Reset session order" returns to automatic sorting. Cards show the time in that status, the last tool used ("after Bash"; only finished tool calls are recorded) or the tool asking for permission, and the last line of the last message. Click a card to focus its tab, in any VS Code window: each window lists the session tabs it opened in `~/.agent-status/windows/<pid>.json`, and a click on a session held by another window brings that window to the front (by opening its folder) and asks it, through `~/.agent-status/focus/<pid>.json`, to show the tab. A card's tooltip says where its session runs; a session started by hand outside the toolkit's tabs only gets a message. Hide a card with its eye icon until the session's next event; closing a tab hides its card too. Hidden cards are listed in the collapsed "Hidden" group at the bottom of the view, where the eye button shows one again; hiding is remembered across reloads.

The hooks are installed with `node <clone>/status/install.mjs` (see [INSTALL.md](INSTALL.md)); it backs up `~/.claude/settings.json` first and adds only its own entries, and `--uninstall` removes them. A small synchronous start-up hook (`status/turn-status-hook.mjs`) asks every interactive session to end each turn with `STATUS: QUESTION` or `STATUS: DONE`. "Toolkit: Open Claude here on startup" opens a plain `claude` tab (session `<project>-claude`, no agent, plugin or prompt) whenever the folder opens; "Toolkit: Stop opening Claude here" turns off both the plain tab and the coordinator for the folder.

The event hook (`status/status-hook.mjs`) runs asynchronously, so sessions never wait for it, and appends one line per event to `~/.agent-status/sessions/<session_id>.jsonl`; errors go to `~/.agent-status/hook.log`. It deletes a session's file at `SessionEnd` and leaves a `<session_id>.ended` marker so late background events cannot bring the session back (a new start or resume clears it), and, when a session starts, removes files and markers idle for more than 6 hours (`STALE_HOURS` at the top of the script). Headless sessions (`claude -p`, SDK, SDD's reviewer) are skipped by the observed but undocumented `CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT=sdk-*` value; `tests/status-entrypoint.e2e.mjs` checks it against the installed CLI. A denied permission stays red until the turn ends, because Claude Code fires no event for a denial.

## Plugin delivery

The organization's managed Claude Code policy currently allows only the official Anthropic marketplace, so the plugin is loaded from the clone with `--plugin-dir` (the extension does it; by hand: `claude --plugin-dir <clone>/plugins/toolkit`). Update with `git pull`, then reload VS Code.

Once an admin allows the marketplace:

```
claude plugin marketplace add dserri/claude-toolkit
claude plugin install toolkit@claude-toolkit
```

and enable auto-update for `claude-toolkit` in `/plugin` → Marketplaces. The plugin declares no version, so every pushed commit is a release.

## Roll back

Delete the `dserri.claude-toolkit-0.0.1` junction and reload VS Code; remove a project's `.coord/` folder if you no longer want its board. Sessions started by hand work as before.

## Develop

```
node --test
node --test tests/coordinator.e2e.mjs tests/status-entrypoint.e2e.mjs
```

The first runs the unit, hook, installer and `claude plugin validate` tests (`claude` must be on `PATH`). The second starts real headless sessions with a model call. Tab behaviour and the session view in VS Code are verified by hand.

# Design

## Context

See proposal.md. The view uses `registerTreeDataProvider`; groups and cards are sorted by `byUrgency`. VS Code supports reordering through a `TreeDragAndDropController` passed to `createTreeView`.

## Decisions

- **Order as key lists** in `globalState` key `sessionOrder` = `{ projects: [project], sessions: { [project]: [session key] } }`. A titled session's key is its name (stable across restarts); an untitled one, named after its folder and not unique, is keyed `id:<session id>` (found in review).
- **Reorders merge, never replace** (found in review): the new list is the displayed keys merged with stored keys not displayed (each kept after its stored predecessor), so hidden sessions and projects without live sessions keep their place.
- **Keyboard alternative** (found in review): "Move up" / "Move down" in the context menu of sessions and projects (reachable with Shift+F10) apply the same move as a drag.
- **Unreadable files** (found in review): `vscode/session-files.js` reports files without parsed events separately, and pruning keeps their hidden entries.
- **Pure helpers in `status-core.js`:** `applyOrder(items, keys, keyOf, fallback)` puts items whose key is listed first in list order, then the rest by `fallback`; `moveBefore(keys, moved, target)` returns the keys with `moved` placed before `target`, or last when `target` is absent. On a drop the view takes the keys as currently displayed, moves one, and stores the full list, so everything displayed becomes placed.
- **Drag and drop:** `createTreeView` with a controller using one mime type for this view; the drag carries the dragged element's kind, project and name; drops are accepted only session→session or session→own project (same project) and project→project.
- **Reset:** command clears `sessionOrder`.
- **Review fixes:** one `persist(key, value)` helper awaits the update, refreshes, and shows an error message if it fails; `readSessions` skips files with no parsed events; the hidden group label becomes `Hidden (n)`.

## Risks / Trade-offs

- [Two sessions with the same name in different projects] → order lists are per project, so names only need to be unique within a project, which session names are.

# Proposal

## Why

The developer wants to arrange the session view as they work: projects in their own order and sessions inside a project in their own order, instead of the automatic urgency sort that, for example, lifts an idle session they rarely use.

## What Changes

- Sessions can be dragged to a new position inside their project, and projects can be dragged among projects; a session cannot be dropped into another project.
- The developer's order wins over urgency. Colours, the status-bar jump and the next-waiting shortcut keep finding waiting sessions. Sessions and projects never placed by hand appear after the placed ones, sorted by urgency.
- "Toolkit: Reset session order" returns to automatic sorting.
- The order is stored per machine and shared by all windows.
- Fixes from the hidden-group review: storage writes report failures; an unreadable or empty session file no longer counts as new activity; the hidden group label reads "Hidden (n)".

## Capabilities

### New Capabilities

None.

### Modified Capabilities

- `session-status`: manual ordering and the review fixes.

## Impact

`vscode/status-core.js`, `vscode/sessions-view.js`, `vscode/package.json`, tests, README.

# Spec Delta

## ADDED Requirements

### Requirement: Manual order

The developer SHALL be able to drag a session onto another session of the same project to place it before that session, or onto its own project to place it last, and drag a project onto another project to place it before. Drops across projects or onto the hidden group SHALL change nothing. The resulting order SHALL be stored per machine, shared by all windows, and SHALL take precedence over urgency; sessions and projects never placed SHALL follow the placed ones in urgency order. "Toolkit: Reset session order" SHALL clear it. "Move up" and "Move down" in the context menu of a session or project SHALL make the same moves without dragging. A reorder SHALL keep the placement of items not currently displayed, and sessions without a title SHALL be ordered individually.

#### Scenario: Reorder sessions

- **WHEN** the developer drags `portal-docs` onto `portal-tester` in the `rehlko-portal` group
- **THEN** `portal-docs` is shown just before `portal-tester` and stays there when statuses change

#### Scenario: Reorder projects

- **WHEN** the developer drags the `api` project onto `rehlko-portal`
- **THEN** `api` is shown before `rehlko-portal` in every window

#### Scenario: Cross-project drop

- **WHEN** the developer drops a `rehlko-portal` session onto an `api` session
- **THEN** nothing moves

#### Scenario: New session

- **WHEN** a new session starts in a project whose sessions were placed by hand
- **THEN** it appears after the placed sessions

#### Scenario: Reset

- **WHEN** the developer runs "Toolkit: Reset session order"
- **THEN** projects and sessions are sorted by urgency again

### Requirement: Robust hidden state

Storage writes for hidden state and order SHALL report a failure to the developer instead of failing silently. A session file that cannot be read or holds no events SHALL NOT be treated as new activity. The hidden group SHALL be labelled "Hidden (n)".

#### Scenario: Unreadable file

- **WHEN** a hidden session's file cannot be read during a refresh
- **THEN** it stays hidden

# Tasks

## 1. Implementation

- [x] 1.1 Add `applyOrder` and `moveBefore` to `vscode/status-core.js` with tests
- [x] 1.2 Drag and drop controller, stored order, reset command, review fixes in `sessions-view.js`/`package.json`; verify VS Code loads it
- [x] 1.3 Document ordering in README

## 2. Acceptance

- [x] 2.1 With the developer: reorder sessions within a project and projects, see a cross-project drop refused, see the order in a second window, reset

findings.summary: vscode/sessions-view.js readSessions now drops files with no parsed events, so an unreadable hidden session is absent from `all`; refresh() then calls status.pruneHidden(stored, all), which keeps only entries of present sessions, and persists the pruned map. On the next refresh with a readable file the session has no hidden entry and appears visible, violating the 'Unreadable file: stays hidden' scenario (e.g. transient Windows sharing violation while the hook appends). Keep hidden entries for ids whose files were skipped (or prune only by file absence) and add a regression test through the readSessions/refresh path; current tests cover only pure helpers.

Order lists are keyed by session.name (status-core orderedGroups, sessions-view drop). Untitled sessions are named after their folder and latestPerTitle does not merge them, so two hand-started sessions in rehlko-portal are both 'rehlko-portal'. Dragging one moves both (moveBefore removes all equal keys), dropping one onto its twin always places it last (target removed from `without`), and duplicate keys are stored. This contradicts design.md's premise that names are unique within a project. Key untitled sessions by id (titled by name) and add a duplicate-name test.

SessionsProvider.drop builds the new projects/sessions list from this.groups (visible only) and overwrites the stored list.
